articleTitle: IDI to Enhance the Longevity of the Knowledge Bases Established on Scoring Systems
abstract: The Integrated Decision Intelligence (IDI) approach helps to improve decision-making processes, minimising the constraints. The integrated approach offers tangible benefits such as improved decision accuracy and risk management, thus addressing the stringent needs of contemporary society. This article represents some intermediate results on the proposed topic, with the authors' focus on the study of the potential of the IDI approach, addressing the shortcomings of conventional scoring systems in the decision-making process and proposing solutions to overcome the limitations and challenges of traditional scoring systems by IDI approach. The domain of clinical medical diagnostics was selected as the primary one for application and testing. The use of algorithms, methods and models specific to the systems based on expert professional knowledge (knowledge based systems) and to the systems based on data processing (data-driven decision making), with further integration, indicates an innovative perspective in this decision science sub-domain.

articleTitle: Head-Level Obstacle Detector for Visually Impaired
abstract: Head-Ievel obstacle detector appears to be a helpful aid for the visually impaired. The detector is ultrasound-based and is used with a white cane. The chest was identified to be the best option for fixing. Testing had two phases, indoor and outdoor, both with visually impaired end users. In phase 1, indoor testing was conducted in a gym using a route with ten artificial obstacles. We found the method to be safe for verifying the functionality of the sensor and mounting. It was also found to be an effective method for learning how to use the device. Indoor testing has shown that the device also reliably detects narrow horizontal obstacles (simulation of branches) at a head level. It also does not detect obstacles on the sides of the user that do not directly threaten him, and so it does not cause unnecessary feedback that would distract the user. Importantly, we did not find any false positive detections. However, the stabilization of the fixing needs to be improved. In phase 2, the outdoor testing, five blind used the detector for four weeks in their everyday life. This method did not provide information about the reliability of detection (the blind do not see it) but indicated a good recognizability of the feedback and good wearability. All blind testers have seen benefits in using the detector.

articleTitle: Classifying Mental Disabilities from Virtual Reality Behavioral Data using Machine Learning
abstract: This study explores the use of Virtual Reality (VR) environments to analyze movement and gaze patterns in subjects with and without mental disorders, including Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) A sample of 72 participants was categorized into typical, ASD-related, and other disorders groups. Three VR experiments were conducted to collect data on movement, gaze, and interaction patterns. The results show distinct behavioral differences between typical and atypical groups, further analyzed using machine learning algorithms-Support Vector Machine, Decision Trees, and Random Forest. While Random Forest excelled in binary classifications, Decision Trees outperformed in multi-class scenarios. Results suggest that VR-based analysis of movement and gaze can enhance the early and accurate diagnosis of mental disorders.

articleTitle: Application Development for Personalized Cancer Treatment
abstract: A promising new direction of personalized medicine is the inclusion of predictive models in the treatment. Such models can help in dose optimization or predictive evolution simulation. The present research presented the design and implementation of an application to facilitate doctors' work by increasing diagnosis accuracy and treatment optimization using mathematical models of tumors. The prediction of tumor progression is based on mathematical models developed using data from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) measurements. In order to take into account also the memory effects of the tumor, it is used the fractional order model. The pilot application is a good start for a more complex personalized medicine tool.

articleTitle: Validation of Blaze-Pose as Model in the Analysis of Lower Extremities During Gait
abstract: The concept of healthcare is being transformed with the introduction of technologies such as computer vision. Recent advances have proven that computer vision implementations result as efficient and cost-effective solution for applications such as clinical gait analysis. Those, the objective of this research was to validate a computer vision-based human pose detection model named Blaze Pose, in its application for gait detection and angular analysis of the lower extremities in comparison with the manual parameter extraction using a biomechanical analysis software Kinovea. For this, the study emphasizes in walking task, specifically the joint angulations (hip, knee and ankle) observed from the lateral side. The results demonstrate that it is feasible to obtain joint angulations using the human pose estimation model. However, significant discrepancies in the results were found when comparing the ankle joint estimation, but there was a relevant similarity in the hip and knee joints; a 37% and 34% percentage error was also observed in the angular measurements obtained. This result indicates that improve in the model must be made to be able to apply it as a tool in clinical assessment o biomechanics.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Benefits of the Tele-Visit Services in Pain Therapy
abstract: Nowadays, telemedicine is increasingly recognized as a promising tool for healthcare delivery. It improves access to medical care while reducing the need for travel. Additionally, tele-visits help reduce overcrowding in healthcare facilities and enhance productivity. The main aim of this study is to evaluate the benefits that both patients and healthcare facilities gain from the tele-visit service offered by the National Cancer Institute G. Pascale (Naples, Italy) in the context of Pain Therapy, with a focus on the economic and organizational aspects of the service. The findings confirm that patients and caregivers save time and costs, simultaneously improving the environmental impact. Besides, they indicate that telemedicine has the potential to significantly improve healthcare delivery and, more broadly, enhance patients' quality of life. Again, the integration of advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence and Machine Learning, could further enhance the capabilities of this service, ensuring personalized care pathways and greater resource optimization. However, certain limitations emerge that hinder the widespread adoption of telemedicine in our country.

articleTitle: Simulation of Comfort Behavior During the Gait Cycle of People with Low Vision
abstract: This paper presents a simulation of the gait cycle of a person with visual impairments. By incorporating sensory deficits into gait models, we investigate changes in walking behavior, balance, and gait mechanics. Data obtained from the simulation were used to analyze essential gait parameters. The results reveal significant differences in gait parameters, such as slower walking speeds and increased reliance on sensory compensation. This simulation offers valuable insights for developing assistive technologies and rehabilitation solutions aimed at improving mobility for individuals with visual impairments

articleTitle: EMC and EMI Issues of Mixed Sensor - Control Boards for Medical Devices
abstract: With the growing use of mixed sensor-control boards in medical devices, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and electromagnetic interference (EMI) represent critical design challenges. For patient safety and device reliability, it is essential that these systems be immune to electromagnetic interference while maintaining the integrity of analog sensor signals. This work examines how an operational amplifier (OP AMP) circuit performs when high-frequency, high current switching signals are used in conjunction with different PWM duty cycles (0%, 20%, 40%, 80%, and 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) in a circuit for medical applications. The sensor impedances are 55 Ω, 0.96 kΩ, 9.83 kΩ. Four different PCB layouts are measured, and the results show design optimizations for improving EMC and reducing EMI. The conclusion of this study is that, before manufacturing, one needs to test several PCB designs, obtained with different design tools, for determining the best design.

articleTitle: Leveraging ResNet-50 for Precision Toxicity Classification in Plants: A Vision-Based Approach to Safeguard Public Health
abstract: The classification of toxic and non-toxic plants plays an important role in ensuring public safety, especially in agriculture, food safety, and health. Correct identification of these plants can prevent accidental poisoning and promote ecological protection. In this paper, we investigate the application of the ResNet-50 model for the classification of toxic and non-toxic plants. Leveraging the powerful feature extraction techniques of the ResNet-50 architecture, the model achieved 89.6% accuracy, 87.4% precision, 91.1% recall, and an 89.2% F1 score, demonstrating the model's effectiveness. Transfer learning proved effective with limited data while maintaining high performance metrics in the classification task. Future research could focus on expanding the dataset to include more plant species and exploring other state-of-the-art models to improve classification accuracy. Additionally, integrating these models with mobile applications or monitoring systems could provide solutions for business and public use, enhancing environmental protection and public safety.

articleTitle: Robotic Assisted Immersive Therapy System for Stroke Rehabilitation
abstract: The number of stroke cases has increased dramatically in the last 30 years, and more and more people are left disabled because of stroke. It is vital to continue researching new ways to recover and improve their condition. Rehabilitation therapies are based on intensive and repeated training starting as soon as possible. However, the number of therapists is too few to treat the growing number of stroke survivors. Advanced technologies such as virtual reality (VR) and robot-assisted therapies have been introduced to improve stroke rehabilitation. VR-based rehabilitation immerses patients in simulated environments, providing visual feedback miming real-world activities. This approach motivates patients through interactive tasks while engaging their cognitive processes, which is crucial for neuroplasticity and motor recovery. Robot-assisted therapy complements VR by providing precise, repetitive movements and proprioceptive feedback. This paper presents a virtual reality- based and robotic-assisted upper limb neuromotor recovery system. The system combines VR immersion with robotic assistance, allowing patients to receive real-time guidance and support during exercise. The system adapts to the patient's condition, providing personalized visual and physical feedback to help relearn motor skills.

articleTitle: Enhancing Antibiotic Stewardship with Power BI Visualization Dashboards: A User Experience Evaluation
abstract: As patient numbers rise, managing antibiotic usage and adhering to Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) guidelines becomes increasingly challenging for healthcare professionals. This study integrates Power BI with Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) to create an Antibiotic Utilization Dashboard, transforming Electronic Health Records (EHR) data into actionable insights. By standardizing data and using interactive visualizations, the dashboard enhances quick-response decision-making, tracks antibiotic trends, and monitors resistance patterns. A five-year dataset was processed in Python and visualized with Power BI, yielding a tool that supports ASP compliance. User feedback via the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) showed strengths in Attractiveness and Efficiency but noted security as an area for improvement. To address this, future work includes transitioning the database to MySQL for better data security. This system offers a valuable approach to improving antibiotic stewardship in healthcare settings.

articleTitle: The Role of Digitalization in the Development of Activities Oriented to Increase the Quality of Life
abstract: Technical-scientific progress has determined the methodology of transforming the innovative economy with the help of digitalization, including public health, one of the main directions of research that is becoming more and more current. This process leaves an increasingly strong impact on the quality of life of the population and its components. The perspectives of the Republic of Moldova integration into the EU put forward new requirements, including in the field of public health. The development of an accessible, safe and inclusive digital environment leads to the population well-being through resilient communication methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Psychophysiological State in Psychologists vs. Tablet-Based Administration of the Mini-Mental Test Through Thermal Imaging
abstract: Dementia affects millions of people worldwide, placing a significant burden on healthcare systems. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for managing the disease, with clinical tests like the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) playing a key role. To alleviate pressure on healthcare resources and support telemedicine, remote administration of such tests through artificial agents must be explored. However, different administration modalities may evoke varying psychophysiological responses in patients. This study aims to evaluate the feasibility of administering the MMSE via a tablet and compare the psychophysiological responses elicited by tablet-based and psychologist-led administration. Contactless technologies, such as thermography, are used to measure these responses, providing valuable insight into stress and engagement. The Wilcoxon signed rank test delivered a lower engagement state (zval=-3.895, p=9.84·10-5) during the psychologist-administered MMSE when compare with the tablet-based administration. The study explores the potential for tablet-based MMSE administration, demonstrating its reliability and fostering the shifting to digital methods.

articleTitle: Sensory Properties of CuO/Cu2O Nanostructures Coated with Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks
abstract: In this work, the sensory response of CuO/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O nanostructures coated with zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIF-71) prepared by low-cost chemical synthesis method in solution is investigated. The process of preparing the studied nanostructures, the study of their response to UV (ultraviolet) and gas, as well as morphological investigations using XRD (X-ray diffraction) and SEM (scanning electron microscopy) of the obtained nanostructures are described. The results of this work describe the sensory response of these nanostructures to UV radiation at room temperature, tested at different operating voltages, and at high temperatures up to 350°C the response to different gases, volatile organic compounds with a concentration of 100 ppm, especially hydrogen which is considered as an environmentally friendly fuel.

articleTitle: Ophthalmic Lenses Assessment for Ultraviolet Radiation Protection
abstract: The protection of the visual system against harmful light radiation is a very important goal of the prevention process developed by optometrists and also by the manufacturers of eyeglass lenses. Therefore, it is important to identify, for each individual case, the best solutions related to the construction of spectacle lenses. Thus, in the first part of the paper are presented general aspects related to the process of propagation of light radiation through the processes of refraction and reflection, and, that is to the luminous radiation propagation efficiency and to the mechanic behavior of the lenses. In the second part of the paper is presented experimental setup for the optical and mechanic investigation of the behavior of a sample of ophthalmic lenses. In the final part of the paper are presented results and conclusions of this spectrometer and microscopic analysis that highlights aspects set as analysis objectives.

articleTitle: Development of an Orthopedic Insole with Pressure Sensors for Automated Assessment of Flat Foot in Children
abstract: Flatfoot is a common condition primarily affecting children, in which the arch of the foot does not develop properly, which can lead to pain and gait problems. Traditionally, orthopedists evaluate this condition using devices such as a podoscope, which rely on subjective observation to determine the degree of flatfoot, and the arch height needed for an appropriate orthotic insole. This approach, however, has limitations due to its imprecision and variability among clinicians. The present study aims to develop a prototype orthotic insole equipped with pressure sensors to determine the degree of arch in flatfoot patients, focusing on children aged 5 to 10 years. The prototype integrates resistive sensors connected to a microcontroller, which collects pressure data on the arch of the foot, which are processed by software to generate an accurate analysis. The results obtained are compared with traditional methods, showing high accuracy in detecting the degree of flatfoot, providing objective data for the development of customized orthopedic insoles.

articleTitle: SnakeMaker A Preview of A User-Friendly Tool For Biomedical Data Processing
abstract: Biomedical data analysis often relies on complex computational steps, leading to pipelines that are challenging to reproduce and share. These scripts, while powerful, can be difficult to understand and modify, especially for researchers with limited programming experience. This lack of transparency deteriorates collaboration and impedes the verification of scientific findings. To address this, we introduce SnakeMaker, a novel tool that simplifies the creation of reproducible and shareable workflows using the Snakemake workflow management system. SnakeMaker parses a set of user-friendly configuration files that specify inputs, outputs, parameters, and shell commands (or custom Python functions), automatically generating a complete Snakemake workflow. This approach significantly reduces the complexity of workflow definition, while enhancing transparency and reproducibility. By enabling easier workflow creation, sharing, and execution, SnakeMaker aims to foster collaboration and improve the reliability of neuroimaging research. The tool's modular design also allows for the creation and sharing of specialized ”forks” tailored to specific analysis pipelines, promoting a community-driven approach to workflow development. SnakeMaker has the potential to be a valuable resource for the scientific community, facilitating robust and reproducible research practices.

articleTitle: Implementation of European Public Environmental Policies in the Context of Improving Public Health
abstract: Studying the impact of environmental factors on quality of life and public health is crucial. Biodiversity is vital for public health, and environmental protection policies are mandatory worldwide. Managing European directives in national public policies enhances environmental quality, positively impacting public health. Sustainable development and economic resilience are key determinants of this relationship. The study analyzed environmental factors using eco-diagnostics and pollution impact assessments. International statistics from organizations like the WHO, World Bank, Environment Agency, and data on environmental quality indicators were used. European directives relevant to environmental management were also considered. A diverse sample of countries was selected based on population and regional homogeneity. Pollution reduction improves the environment and indirectly increases life expectancy, supporting sustainable development and protecting public health. The Republic of Moldova promotes environmental protection through initiatives like tree planting, organic agriculture, water resource management, and renewable energy development. The pollution index in researched countries confirms that polluted environments affect population health by increasing mortality rates. For instance, countries like Portugal, Italy, Ukraine, Albania, Bulgaria, and Romania have higher pollution indices, which negatively impact life expectancy. The authors aimed to assess the extent of national economic and societal development through environmental pollution reduction methods. The research reconciles economic and social development with environmental improvement, enhancing population quality of life. It highlights the multifaceted nature of environmental management, influenced by each country's economic model and pollution levels. Despite differences, countries share responsibility for implementing environmental protection policies.

articleTitle: Emotion Detection from Face Images Using Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Face Emotions Recognition (FER) systems are becoming increasingly performant, benefiting from developments in computer vision and deep learning techniques. In this paper, a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model is proposed for classifying facial expressions into three primary emotion categories: positive, neutral, and negative. The designed custom architecture integrates residual connections, which enhance the model's ability to generalize by effectively retaining learned features across layers. The proposed model achieves an average accuracy of 92.16%, demonstrating good performances in discriminating between data from each targeted class. The FER2013 and its curated version, FER Plus, datasets were employed for training and testing different models. A new subset of FER Plus was created for model training and testing. Various preprocessing techniques were applied, including data normalization, augmentation and class balancing.

articleTitle: Exploring Dunbar's Number Through COVID-19: Analyzing Daily Testing and Case Dynamics in Dunbar-Sized Groups and Their Impact on Twitter Sentiment via Granger Causality
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic enables the exploration of traditional psycho-sociological concepts, such as Dunbar's number, which suggests a limit of about 150 people with whom an individual can maintain stable social relationships, although estimates vary. In this study, we provide a new estimate of Dunbar's number by analyzing COVID-19 datasets from 2020 - before vaccines were available - focusing on the dynamics of daily testing and positive cases. We investigated sentiment changes in time using a large corpus of English-written, COVID-19-related tweets from Twitter. Our approach involved calculating the sizes of virtual population groups that theoretically include just one individual who was tested or tested positive. In the first year of COVID-19, many individuals did not fully believe in the existence or serious impacts of the disease - thus, knowing at least one positive case could influence them to accept the severe reality and, potentially, express their sentiment on Twitter. The knowledge of at least one such individual within one's Dunbar circle could lead to more negative sentiment in tweets. The larger Dunbar's number is, i.e., the more people an individual could know well, the easier it is to know at least one new tested or positive case. Employing Granger causality, we compared the sizes of groups with at least one tested individual against various hypothetical values of Dunbar's number to estimate the minimum number of connections necessary within such groups. Our findings suggest that Dunbar's number could be about 175, which aligns closely with the traditionally cited figure of 150.

articleTitle: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Detection Through Video Sequences: A Transformer-Based Approach for e-Health Application
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for detecting Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) using a Stochastic Transformer architecture specifically designed to process video sequence data. Utilizing the ‘PTSD-in-the-wild’ dataset, which consists of 613 interviews from individuals with and without PTSD, the model efficiently captures spatio-temporal features through 3D convolutional tubelet embedding and stochastic layers to enhance generalization and reduce overfitting. Key innovations include the use of a stochastic LWTA layer within the Transformer, allowing the model to perform with high accuracy (0.91), recall (0.92), and F1-score (0.90) compared to a baseline model. This study highlights the promising applications of advanced machine learning algorithms, particularly deep learning, in analyzing video data to aid in the diagnosis of mental health conditions in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Knowledge Fusion Through Ambient Smart Living Technology and Telemonitoring in Emergency Response
abstract: With the help of knowledge fusion methods, it is possible to interconnect different sources of knowledge, enhancing the individual knowledge fields, enabling to connect various, compatible kinds of systems for the purposes of decision-making or tailored recommendations. Especially in the field of healthcare and medicine, such advancements can support health professionals in providing patient-driven, fast and accurate treatments. For this, a common ground is needed where data can be stored and accessed in real time. This, in addition to medical digital services, will help facilitating a timely analysis of specific patients. Particularly, the concept of a digital twin (DT) is suitable to help and is profiting from a knowledge fusion perspective. This paper focuses on the idea of merging ambient smart living technologies with health parameters (such as vital signs) to develop a DT -concept, integrated into rescue operations as a DT -service. An alarm event detected by this DT, such as a heart attack, can lead then to an early rescue operation, resulting in a fast treatment of the patient. In this paper, a concept for the use of a DT and DT services, combined with the use of knowledge fusion will be elaborated in detail.

articleTitle: Utilization of Hermetia Illucens (Linnaeus,1758) as an Alternative Feed in Aquatic and Terrestrial Zootechny: Implications for Sustainable Food Production and Human Health Safety
abstract: The cosmopolitan dipteran Hermetia illucens (Linnaeus, 1758), also known as black soldier fly, has emerged as a promising alternative feed ingredient in both aquatic and terrestrial animal farming due to its high nutritional value and low environmental impact. This article explores its potential to enhance sustainability in zootechny—both aquatic and terrestrial—and its broader implications for global food security. Also, this paper examines the safety and health impacts associated with using insect-based feeds on human health, focusing on the risk of allergens, bioaccumulation of toxins, and foodborne diseases. By examining existing research and case studies, the findings suggest that zootechnical products derived from Hermetia illucens-fed aquatic and terrestrial animals offer enhanced nutritional benefits and lower environmental impact, with promising implications for human health. Nevertheless, further research is needed to explore long-term effects and optimize feed formulations for maximum benefit.

articleTitle: Ultrasound Breast Phantom for Breast Biopsy Training
abstract: Ultrasound-guided breast biopsy is an important part of the examination chain for breast cancer. However, adequate training for such interventions is limited. This work focuses on creating an anthropomorphic breast phantom suitable for ultrasound-guided intervention training. For this purpose, a computer model of a breast was generated, which was subsequently converted to an STL file and 3D printed using a fused filament fabrication (FFF) 3D printer. The 3D-printed breast model was utilized as a mold for constructing the phantom, which is primarily made from soft and flexible silicone rubber. Additionally, the phantom includes several tumor entities. An experienced radiologist evaluated the breast phantom. Although the depth of ultrasound penetration was limited, the core-needle biopsy test proved promising as well as the visual and tactile simulation. Furthermore, the manufacturing costs can be considered low.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis on Solid Ankle-Foot Orthosis with Additive Manufacturing Materials
abstract: Additive manufacturing shows substantial potential for future advancements in the design and production of ankle-foot orthoses, crucial in the treatment of neuromusculoskeletal conditions. This research compares 3D printing materials and thickness of AFOs using CAD simulations. Various 3D printing materials were evaluated, analyzing density variations. The results showed that polypropylene exhibited a maximum stress of 9,404 MPa in the thinnest model, which decreased with thickness. PLA showed high stress in thin models but improved with thickness, while ABS and Nylon 101 had intermediate values. PLA demonstrated low displacements, indicating superior resistance to deformation, and total deformation results emphasized its ability to withstand loading without excessive deformation. Mechanical stiffness analysis highlighted material specific differences, with PLA exhibiting high stiffness, particularly in thick models, and Nylon 101 consistently showing higher values than other materials. This innovative approach has the potential to develop an effective and personalized AFO, enhancing the quality of life of patients with neuromusculoskeletal conditions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Liposomal Stability on Spontaneous Oxidation by Spectroscopic Methods
abstract: Phosphatidylcholine-based liposomes obtained by the thin film hydration method were subjected to different homogenization treatments. Properties of relevant samples were analyzed in terms of size and ζ-potential. Moreover, the stability in time concerning spontaneous oxidation was investigated by spectroscopic means to assess the potential for further use in drug loading and the formulation shelf-life.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Mapping of Irritative Network in Focal Cortical Dysplasia: Sorting Multifocal Interictal Epileptiform Discharges
abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IED) are an electrophysiological hallmark of epilepsy, and their occurrence characterizes brain tissue that is connected to the epileptic network of focal epilepsy - irritative zone (IZ). IZ is composed of partially overlapped sub-regions generating IED independently. Various ways of spreading IEDs complicate localization of IED sources resulting in sub-regional fragmentation or insufficient decomposition using signal analysis of stereo-EEG monitoring for surgical treatment of epilepsy. We localized the sources of IED for each sub-region of highly fragmented IZ resulting from the previously published algorithm. To identify and merge sub-regions having the same IED source, we designed and optimized an iterative algorithm using additional spatial coordinates of all intracranial EEG recording contacts. Forty-four patients with focal cortical dysplasia (FCD), who underwent epilepsy surgery, were analyzed to find criteria for maximal reduction in the number of sub-regions while maintaining clinically relevant IZ decomposition. The optimal Euclidian distance between any IED sources that result in the merging of sub-regions was found at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{R}=10.6 \mathbf{m}\mathbf{m}$</tex>. The approach used significantly reduced the number of the sub-regions to six at the median <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{p}=0.004$</tex>, U-test) with a lower mutual overlap of 10.7 % (p<0.002, U-test). The presented method reduces the sub-regional fragmentation of IZ and maintains a detailed description of the epileptic network. It facilitates the advance of detailed analysis of the interaction between epileptic focus, IED generators, and the effect of their removal by surgery in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Networks Trained with Eccentric and Concentric Cylinders to Estimate the Electric Fields
abstract: Estimation of radiofrequency electric fields is of great importance in Magnetic Resonance Imaging to estimate Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) and SNR in tissues. In order to develop a quick patient-specific estimation of SAR, recent publications have shown that use of deep learning networks can provide a valid alternative to numerical electromagnetic simulations, which can be time consuming. Analytical solutions have the benefit of providing an exact distribution of the fields in a very short time, therefore they can be suitable to generate large amounts of data for deep learning networks training. On the other hand, analytical solutions can be calculated only for simple specific geometries. In this work, we explore the ability of three neural networks to estimate the distribution of the electric fields when a B, map is used as an input. The networks were trained with only data generated through analytical solutions representing the fields of eccentric and concentric infinitely long cylinders excited by an infinitely long wire. The networks could predict the fields calculated with the analytical solutions with a very high accuracy also when tested with geometries not part of the training dataset. Hence, the networks can well generalize the transformation from B1 maps to electric fields and the analytical solutions can be used as an alternative data augmentation method for datasets comprising more complicated and heterogeneous structures with the fields are computed with numerical solutions.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Detection Using Constrained Neural Networks and the Development of an Optimized Technical Infrastructure for Resource-Efficient Diagnosis
abstract: This work addresses the challenge of detecting skin cancer from dermatological images using artificial intelligence. The focus is on exploring the potential of lightweight convolutional neural networks to develop efficient diagnostic tools that can function on portable, resource-constrained devices, ensuring accessibility for medical personnel. A comparison of several TinyML models is presented, considering both diagnostic accuracy and computational demands. Some recently introduced models (V-CNN and VRES-CNN) were evaluated against the well-established EfficientN et or ResN et and the results indicated certain advantages for the recent models. Particularly, a quantization technique applied to V-CNN and VRES-CNN was found to further reduce their complexity while maintaining a high accuracy of over 98,5% for the best model.

articleTitle: Case Studies on SMEs in E-Health
abstract: The e-health sector has rapidly evolved over the past decade, driven by the adoption of digital solutions in healthcare and accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have played a significant role in driving innovation, contributing solutions such as telemedicine platforms, wearable health devices, and mobile health applications. Despite facing regulatory, operational, and financial challenges, SMEs have introduced groundbreaking solutions that improve patient care, reduce healthcare costs, and enhance access. This paper explores case studies of companies like Teladoc, Fitbit, and Doxy.me, highlighting their strategies for overcoming challenges in the e-health industry. We also examine broader trends in the digital healthcare landscape and how SMEs continue to shape the future of healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Assessment of Advanced Systems for Managing Difficult Intubation
abstract: This study evaluates the economic impact and efficacy of the “Vivasight” endobronchial intubation device with an integrated camera compared to traditional double-lumen tubes (DLT) during one-lung ventilation in thoracic surgery. The aim is to assess whether Vivasight remains a viable alternative to DLT, as demonstrated in a previous 2017 study. A thorough literature review and a statistical analysis of data collected from thoracic surgeries performed between March and May 2024 were conducted, focusing on primary outcomes such as intubation time and surgical duration, along with secondary outcomes including lung collapse quality, ease of intubation, and postoperative complications. Results indicate that, although Vivasight does not require verification controls, it prolongs average surgical duration and intubation time compared to the 2017 study. No significant differences in postoperative complications like cough and sore throat were found; however, notable reductions in dysphonia, ease of intubation and improved lung collapse, were associated with Vivasight. Economically, Vivasight demonstrates lower costs compared to conventional DLT with two bronchoscopy controls, while remaining comparable to DLT with a single bronchoscopy control. Overall, Vivasight represents a valid alternative from a clinical point of view and effectively standardizes intubation procedure costs.

articleTitle: SpO2 Histograms - Valuable Tools for Assessing Oxygen Saturation Stability of Newborns
abstract: Pulse oximeters are essential devices used in neonatology for non-invasive monitoring of neonatal vital signs. In this group of patients it is essential to monitor the SPO2 parameter, which cannot be low or unphysiologically high. Pulse oximeters commonly provide insight into the so-called SpO2 trend data, which is the SpO2 curve over time. If a patient is evaluated based only on trend values, certain situations may be missed. This paper presents a software tool to process the trends into so-called histograms, which summarize the data and present them more clearly.

articleTitle: Clustering 3D Tracking in Zebrafish Laboratory Trials
abstract: Due to the significant genetic similarities between zebrafish (Danio rerio) and humans, researchers are increasingly utilizing this species to develop novel therapies for various health conditions by analysing their behaviour across healthy and treated subjects. The current workflow in laboratory trials typically involves a small number of fish subjects, leading to simplified behavioural models where One-way ANOV A is often sufficient to meet statistical requirements. In this study, we propose an alternative approach to understanding fish behaviour. Our methodology begins with two datasets of 3D video recordings (95 zebrafish and 80 goldfish samples), followed by the application of the KMeans clustering and HMM (Hidden Markov Models) classification algorithms to time-series data derived from 3D tracking features.

articleTitle: Prototype of a Surgical Template Based On CBCT Scan and Produced with Additive Technology
abstract: The wide availability of 3D printing technologies makes patient-specific treatment more accessible. This study aims at creating a custom prototype device that can improve the visualization and precision of a dental surgical procedure. For this purpose, an intra-oral scanner and a CBCT images were used as a basis for the computer model of the prototype device, while a Low Force Stereolithography 3D printer was used for its physical realization. The prototype was successfully realized and will be further evaluated.

articleTitle: A Computer Vision-Based Solution for Assessing Prosthetic Leg Length Discrepancy
abstract: This paper presents a novel computer vision-based approach for assessing leg length discrepancy (LLD) in individuals with prosthetic limbs. The proposed solution uses image processing techniques to detect markers placed on the patient's knee, prosthesis, and a reference wall, allowing for precise measurement of limb alignment. Through a comparative analysis of the initial reference position, set by a specialist, and the current limb positioning, the algorithm identifies discrepancies in leg length. The system employs a non-invasive methodology, utilizing an IP camera to capture images and communicate them via Wi-Fi to a computing unit for further analysis. Experimental validation, conducted on simulated LLDs ranging from 1mm to 10mm, demonstrates the system's high sensitivity and accuracy in detecting subtle changes in limb alignment. This approach offers a scalable, automated alternative to traditional manual methods, improving both the reliability and ease of prosthetic adjustments.

articleTitle: Contact-Constrained Finite Element Analysis to Evaluate Obstetric Forceps Placement
abstract: Obstetric forceps are frequently used when physiologic childbirth fails to progress. It is commonly accepted in obstetrics that the use of the instrument is safe when placed and handled correctly. Conversely, obstetric forceps may cause significant damage to the fetal scalp, skull bones and brain if they are not applied correctly. In this paper, we assess obstetric forceps placement in-silico by creating virtual models of the fetal head and obstetric forceps. We establish mechanical contact between the fetal scalp and forceps blades. We then run implicit quasi-static Finite Element Analyses to assess the deformation of the fetal scalp when in contact with the forceps blades. Progressive steps are described to arrive at a final simulation that compares the symmetric placement of the forceps blades against their asymmetric placement. We show that the deformation of the fetal head is significantly more problematic when the forceps blades are asymmetrically placed relative to the fetal head.

articleTitle: A Novel Breast Phantom Created Using GPU-Based Voxelization for X-Ray Breast Imaging Research
abstract: Anthropomorphic x-ray medical phantoms are models of the human tissue, organ, system, whole body, created with different purposes, such as optimization of imaging techniques, optimization of dose to the patient, testing reconstruction images for newly developed modalities, as well as performing quality control of x-ray medical devices. In the field of breast imaging, significant efforts have been devoted to developing heterogeneous breast phantoms for use with 3D imaging techniques. It is crucial that both, physical and computational phantoms share identical properties. Anthropomorphic computational phantoms can be derived from patient imaging data or constructed using combinations of geometric primitives. In the latter case, the use of large number of primitives can significantly increase computational complexity, making ray-tracing techniques time-consuming and inefficient, while also complicating the insertion of lesions. This study aims to develop a voxel-based version of a breast mathematical phantom, originally constructed from geometric primitives, to facilitate the efficient generation of x-ray images. The mathematical phantom consists of 15863 geometric primitives, including two semicylinders, one parallelepiped, and the rest spheres of varying diameters. The voxelization process was carried out using a GPU programming approach. X-ray images of both, the mathematical and voxel-based phantoms were generated and compared, with an observed maximum difference of 0.6%, attributed to the voxelization algorithm. Improvements to this algorithm are also planned. The model is suitable for use with various lesions inserted for virtual experiments.

articleTitle: Combining GANs and Federated Learning for Privacy Protection
abstract: The main focus of this paper is to ensure the privacy of customer data, by using defense mechanisms such as GAN s for generating synthetic data and differential privacy. The tests were performed on medical datasets, such as Chest X-Rays, Brain Cancer and Kidney Cancer. We used GANs both to generate more data to increase accuracy by up to 20%, but also to protect client data using entirely synthetic data and reaching a similar accuracy if the number of samples per party is doubled.

articleTitle: Speech Perception and Speech Attention: A Case Study Based on Event-Related Potential Using the OpenBCI System
abstract: Perception and attention to sounds, especially speech, can be one of the most important foundations of learning and establishing social interactions, especially for specific disorders such as autism spectrum disorders. So far, most studies have focused on prosody or syntactic aspects of sentences or individual features of speech sounds, but few studies have comprehensively covered all of these. In this research, we have examined the way sounds are understood by ordinary people in a declarative sentence with 7 different characteristics. These results can be used as a basis for comparing and estimating the amount of language damage in autistic people and, as a result, to design a method for better understanding of these children in educational and communication matters.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Continuous Recognition of Activities of Daily Living
abstract: Pathological tremor, which impairs the ability to perform daily activities, presents challenges for current therapeutic strategies based on subjective clinical assessments and symptomatic management. This paper introduces an innovative system for classifying activities in patients with tremor, using models trained on time series data segmented into different window sizes. The system achieved an overall accuracy of 80%, although performance varied across tasks. This represents a significant advancement in the current state of continuous activity classification systems, highlighting the potential to enhance tremor monitoring and optimize medication dosage.

articleTitle: A Review of Advances in the Dietary Inclusion of Hermetia Illucens in Fish Feeds
abstract: Aquaculture has become increasingly vital in the 21st century, as wild aquatic resources face overexploitation, the global population continues to grow rapidly, and the demand for protein sources rises. Advances in genetic breeding technologies, environmental microbiology, immunology, and nutrition have driven significant breakthroughs in aquaculture, enhancing both production and quality. These innovations are helping to meet the world's growing needs for sustainable and reliable food sources. Insect proteins are anticipated to play a significant role in the animal feed market, particularly in aquaculture, following the EU's 2017 decision to lift the ban on their use in fish feeds. Since then, a nascent industry has gained momentum, accelerating its growth. Research and industry efforts have focused primarily on larvae from a select few insect species, which have garnered the most attention for their potential in this field. Among the organisms most studied in aquaculture are black soldier flies, especially their larvae, which are full of protein (up to 50% of their weight) and can be transformed into a variety of products. This review aims to comprehensively examine and critically review the use of Hermetia illucens in aquaculture.

articleTitle: Research on Advances in Production of Human Dentition and Dental Bridges Using Additive Manufacturing (Metal 3D Printing)
abstract: The paper presents an overview of different parts of the human dentition as well as dental bridges produced through metal additive manufacturing. Until now, the most commonly used materials in dentition and bridge prosthetics include combinations as ceramics, resins, and both precious and non-precious metals due to their specific properties. This field has advanced significantly in dental technology. In addition to traditional wax modeling, teeth and bridges were digitally designed using software like 3 Shape and Exocad. Scanners digitally capture models or receive them directly from intraoral scans. Milling and laser-melting processes ensure precise and safe production, with a wide range of materials available, such as zirconium and other metals. An alternative technology, Additive Manufacturing of metal, also known as metal 3D printing, is the newest process where material is added layer by layer to form three-dimensional components. This process has revolutionized various industries, including medical and dental fields, enabling high precision and flexibility in design and production. The use of metallic materials such as titanium alloys is ideal for creating parts that can be safely implanted in the human body. The use of metallic materials such as titanium alloys is ideal for creating parts that can be safely implanted in the human body.

articleTitle: Novel Activation Function Design for Multiple Sclerosis Detection in Medical Imaging
abstract: The central nervous system is impacted by multiple sclerosis (MS), a chronic and frequently disabling illness that causes a variety of physical and mental disabilities. Effective management and therapy depend heavily on early diagnosis and the ability to anticipate the course of the disease. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) approaches to forecast the onset and course of MS is investigated in this work. The paper introduces a novel function called Gelu Error Activation Function (GERF), that computes Gauss error function (erf) of Gaussian Error Linear Unit (GELU) function. Clinical and imaging data from MS patients make up a large dataset that is used in this research. The data is prepped for analysis using a variety of preprocessing techniques, including as feature extraction, data cleaning, and normalization. Alongside deep learning models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are reviewed. Our results indicate that AI models, particularly those utilizing deep learning techniques, significantly outperform traditional methods in predicting MS. By utilizing GERF, it achieved lowest mean loss (0.1397) and highest mean validation accuracy (94.46<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) of MS predictions. GERF can directly replace Sigmoid, ReLU, tanh, Swish, Nip una, Serf, and GELU in deep neural network architectures. The study highlights how AI has the power to transform MS prediction and diagnosis, opening the door to more individualized treatment plans and improved patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Xenogeneic Small Intestine Submucosa Surface Modification During Processing for Tissue Engineering
abstract: Tissue engineering is an interdisciplinary field of science that uses the principles of health sciences and engineering to develop the biomaterials that can mimic the structure of an organ, with enabling growth factors, control over cell growth to generate tissues for restoration, maintenance or improving the function of the affected organ. Tissue engineering has evolved over time through the development of biopolymer scaffolds with the capacity to stimulate in vitro and in vivo cell growth. Having control over the scaffolds surface, one can improve the cell vitality and proliferation on them. Small intestinal submucosa has been shown to be a promising biological scaffold due to its biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, high biological activity, and biodegradability; its structure is mainly based on collagen derived from the mucosal layer of porcine small intestine. By removing the epithelial layer and decellularization of small intestine submucosa, an acellular matrix is obtained, which possess good regenerative activity. This article discusses methods for modification of the intestine submucosa surface to optimize and improve the biocompatible performance of the materials to adapt to tissue defects with purpose of their regeneration.

articleTitle: Advancing Voice Authentication: Insights from Cepstral Coefficients and Recursive Feature Elimination in Speech Signal
abstract: Voice manipulation and synthesis pose a growing threat to digital security, raising the need for effective systems to detect artificial speech. This study investigates the feasibility of distinguishing between real and synthetic voices through machine learning techniques applied to the Fake or Real (FoR) Dataset from York University. The dataset contains over 70,000 text-to-speech (TTS) recordings, balanced in gender, class, sample rate, volume, and number of channels. The approach utilizes Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GTCC) and Delta Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (AGTCC) as key features for voice characterization. A logistic regression model, enhanced with Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), was employed to identify the most discriminative coefficients for this task. RFE iteratively removed less significant features, enhancing both the performance and interpretability of the model. The final model achieved a 70% accuracy in testing, using only five AGTCC features. This comparative analysis of GTCC and AGTCC revealed their respective strengths in voice classification tasks, offering insights for future developments in voice authentication systems. The study not only advances voice authentication technologies but also highlights the crucial role of feature selection in improving the robustness of models designed to safeguard against synthetic voice threats.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Approaches for Classifying Parkinson's Disease Using fNIRS Data from Gait Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the use of machine learning to differentiate between Parkinson's patients and healthy individuals using functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals collected during walking. fNIRS data, which monitor brain activity, were acquired from both groups to identify distinctive patterns. Using machine learning techniques, the model was trained to discriminate the two classes, with the goal of improving early and non-invasive diagnosis of Parkinson's disease and the method delivered an accuracy of 72.00%. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in accurately distinguishing patients from healthy individuals from cortical activity during walking.

articleTitle: Intraocular Pressure Determining System Based on Rebound Tonometry
abstract: Glaucoma is a common neuropathy that causes irreversible blindness. The main categories of glaucoma are open-angle and closed-angle. Open-angle glaucoma is the most common type and is caused by increased flow resistance through Schlemm's canal. Most cases of open-angle glaucoma are discovered during routine eye exams due to their mainly asymptomatic nature. Intraocular pressure (IOP) is one of the most critical risk factors in diagnosing glaucoma. Tonometry is the procedure of measuring intraocular pressure. Currently, one of the most popular forms of tonometry is rebound tonometry. This paper aims to reproduce the technology behind the rebound tonometer by developing a system that measures the deceleration of a standardized magnetic probe. The system includes a magnetized probe, an electromagnetic propulsion mechanism, and an amplification circuit, with signal processing conducted in real time using a microcontroller and MATLAB. Experimental results demonstrated the system's ability to capture probe deceleration and correlate it with IOP in a simulated medium. The system's performance was evaluated by altering the probe's speed, and the results indicated an apparent variation in induced current relative to probe velocity. However, further optimization is needed to minimize external magnetic interference and increase sampling frequency for improved accuracy. The study lays the groundwork for developing portable and cost-effective rebound tonometers that can provide rapid, non-invasive measurements of IOP.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Medical Data Management with Secure Self-Sovereign Applications for Patient Empowerment
abstract: The digitization of healthcare introduces significant challenges in data privacy, security, and control. Self-sovereign applications (SSAs), powered by blockchain, enable patients to control their medical data in a decentralized manner, addressing these issues. This paper explores the principles of SSAs, their benefits in securing patient data, and challenges to widespread adoption. Showcasing the PharmaLedger clinical trial prototype, we demonstrate the potential of SSAs to securely manage everyday medical data, granting patients full sovereignty over their health information and illustrating SSAs’ role in shaping the future of medical data management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Learning and Therapy for Children with Autism: Innovative Activities with the NAO Robot
abstract: Worldwide, autism affects 1 in 100 children, with diagnoses steadily rising since the 2000s. Romania lacks official statistics on autism prevalence, but global estimates suggest similarity. Children with autism struggle with social interactions and verbal communication, prompting interest in social robots for therapy and education. Tailored robot-assisted sessions offer potential for cognitive development, vocabulary enhancement, social interaction, and behavioral stimulation like concentration and attention. The NAO robot's user-friendly design, technical capabilities, and integrated features make it well-suited for these purposes. This paper presents activities that exemplify the concept of “learning through play,” allowing children to engage in exploration, experimentation, and effective learning in an enjoyable manner.

articleTitle: A Serverless Implementation of a Tool for Temperature and SAR Estimation (TESS 2.0)
abstract: Temperature Estimation from SAR Simulation (TESS) stands as a Cloud-based tool specifically designed for evaluating the safety aspects of MRI examinations. It utilizes a customized version of the bioheat equation, incorporating factors like the temporal changes in body temperature and various physiological parameters in its numerical solutions. Here we present TESS 2.0, with new functionalities and a more user-friendly interface. Notably, the computations occur in a serverless manner, utilizing AWS to enhance efficiency and accessibility.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Investigation of Volleyball Movements Using Electromyography and Visual Tracking Techniques
abstract: In sports, particularly in volleyball, it is very important to study muscular and biomechanical activities to optimize training programs, prevent injuries, and develop personalized rehabilitation protocols. This paper investigates neuromuscular coordination and muscle activation patterns during five key volleyball movements: running, attack, block, reception, and serve. Utilizing surface electromyography (EMG) and visual tracking techniques, we analyzed the activation of the gastrocnemius muscle alongside knee joint kinematics. The Myoware Surface EMG sensor was used to acquire muscle activity data, while a motion tracking system captured the positions of markers placed on the athlete's legs. Two virtual instruments were developed in LabView for data analysis: one for extracting joint angles from video frames, and another for processing EMG signals, including the calculation of RMS values, onset moments, and signal variability. The study highlights the distinct muscle activation profiles across movements, with running and reception showing higher RMS values and greater variability in muscle activation, while attack demonstrated lower and more consistent activation. The correlation between EMG activity and knee joint angle was strongest during block and reception, indicating a greater reliance on precise joint positioning for stability and performance. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the biomechanical demands of volleyball and provide actionable data for improving both performance and injury prevention strategies in athletes.

articleTitle: Brain Computer Interface Controlled Humanoid Robot
abstract: This paper presents a first step towards controlling a neuroprosthesis or an exoskeleton with the power of one's mind. In this experiment, a brain-computer interface was used to control a humanoid robot, achieving an average accuracy of 88.53% across all users. While the outcome is promising, the small sample size limits the strength of any broad conclusions. Plans are underway to increase the number of participants and gather more data. Additionally, the robotic system's delay, which is a notable drawback, is being actively addressed along with other research evaluations in progress.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Real-Time Electrocardiogram Monitoring and Recording System
abstract: This paper presents the development of an loT-based real-time electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring and recording system. The system utilizes an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with an AD8232 ECG sensor and a DS18B20 temperature sensor. Data acquired by the ESP32 is transmitted over the internet using the MQTT protocol to a Raspberry Pi 4 server, where it is processed using Node-RED and stored in an InfluxDB database. The system visualizes the data via Grafana, while a custom HTML interface provides real-time access to users. This design enables remote heart rate and temperature monitoring, facilitating personalized, proactive healthcare management. The implementation ensures real-time data acquisition, analysis, and storage, offering a practical solution for continuous cardiovascular monitoring.

articleTitle: Organoleptic and Physico-chemical Changes of Butter During Storage
abstract: In this study, organoleptic and physico-chemical changes of butter during storage were investigated. Butter samples with different fat contents (65, 78 and 82%) were purchased from the Romanian market. The moisture content was between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15.13 \pm 0.01\%$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$34.43 \pm 0.08\%$</tex> and varied very little during storage. None of the analyzed samples exceeded 2% salt content and the acidity varied between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.22\pm 0.02$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.30\pm 0.06$</tex> ml NaOH n/1 la 100 g. The results showed that the peroxide value increased during storage for all butter samples, while the iodine index increased from values below 25 g <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{2}/100$</tex> g to values above 30 g <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{2}/100$</tex> g. All butter samples were initially colored in the yellow-green range, and during storage the color changes (according to the Kreiss reaction) indicating that the samples are undergoing a rancidity process.

articleTitle: Oxidative Stress Assesmennt in Preterm Premature Rupture Of Membranes (Pprom) — A New Challenge
abstract: Premature rupture of membranes may be caused by a natural weakening of the membranes and it can have its origin in different causes such as infections, high blood pressure or a twin pregnancy and it basically represents a cellular degradation. It is called a premature rupture is it takes place before week 37 of pregnancy. This cellular degradation can be analyzed through the values of the oxidative stress before the PRM. Using machine learning techniques such as Splunk we could predict which is the probability for a certain group age to develop a rupture of the membrane according to the data that we collected, which are the values that can lead to a membrane rupture and for which values there is a high probability for a rupture to occur fits for both the mother and the baby.

articleTitle: Optimization of Parameters for Fluorescent Carbon Nanodots Preparation
abstract: Recently, carbon dots—small carbon-based nanoparticles—have gained popularity as versatile nanomaterials in various biomedical fields, including theranostics and biological sensing. Beyond their remarkable properties, carbon dots are also inexpensive and environmentally friendly to produce. Depending on the desired characteristics, nearly any carbon-containing material can be used as a precursor in their manufacturing. However, the preparation methods for carbon dots face a significant challenge in selecting suitable production process parameters. This work discusses the optimization of the so-called “bottom-up” method and presents the primary characterization of the prepared nanoparticles using DLS and FTIR. By adjusting the process parameters, carbon dots with hydroxyl and amine functional groups and an average size of 2 nm were produced. This optimization has led to the development of a reliable and reproducible bottom-up method, enabling the inexpensive production of carbon dots for use in bioengineering.

articleTitle: Calcium Hydroxide Liners Enhanced with Silver Nanoparticles Doped Hydroxyapatite-Initial Assesment
abstract: Liner materials play crucial roles in modern dentistry by protecting dental pulp, promoting healing, and enhancing the longevity of restorations, thus contributing to successful patient outcomes and overall oral health. By continuing to advance these materials, by the successful combination with other therapeutic agents, dental medicine can improve patient outcomes, enhance the healing process, and increase the longevity of dental treatments. Adding hydroxyapatite (HA) with silver nanoparticles to dental liners combines the advantages of both materials, offering several enhanced benefits as this initial study shows, especially in terms of moisture uptake.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Estimation of POMA Scores from EMG and Kinematic Data in Stroke Patients
abstract: A stroke is a critical medical disease characterized by the abrupt cessation of blood flow to the brain, resulting in cellular injury or necrosis. The effects of stroke on people might range from minor impairments to significant disabilities. Stroke treatment often requires gait rehabilitation. The efficacy of rehabilitative treatment is often assessed using clinical scales. Among them, the Performance-Oriented Mobility Assessment (POMA) is commonly used for assessing balance and gait in stroke patients. Importantly, evaluating muscle activation and kinematic patterns by electromyography (EMG) and stereophotogrammetry during ambulation might provide insights into gait impairments. This study intends to use a machine learning-based regression to predict the POMA total score using EMG and kinematic data in stroke patients. The model achieved correlations of 0.70 and 0.67 throughout the validation and testing stages, respectively. The t-test indicated no bias between the estimated and measured POMA values, but the Bland-Altmann plot revealed a systematic error in the model. Although preliminary, these results indicate the potential to construct models that might provide significant assistance to clinicians by offering accurate evaluations of motor deficits reported post-stroke.

articleTitle: nnU-Net: Investigation of Attention Mechanism for Prostate Zone Segmentation Task
abstract: Prostate cancer is one of the deadliest cancers globally, and early diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. An important step in diagnosing prostate cancer involves segmenting prostate zones in magnetic resonance images. The method achieving the most accurate results when solving this task the no-new U-Net. This study proposes several modifications of this method. These modifications consist of replacing a classical U-Net architecture, used in no-new U-Net, with Grid Attention U-Net, Dual-Attention U-Net and Multi-Dimensional Attention U-Net architectures. The original no-new U-Net method is compared with the proposed modifications. The experimental results show that the proposed modifications generalize worse than the standard no-new U-Net method. Meanwhile, there is no significant difference between achieved accuracies of the compared methods.

articleTitle: Life Cycle Assessment of Chicken Meat Production: a Romanian Case Study
abstract: The aim of this paper was to assess the environmental impact of the slaughtering and preparation of chicken meat in a Romanian company, following a “gate-to-gate” approach. The functional unit chosen was 1 kg of chicken meat. Input and output data were collected from the industry, considering 2022 as the reference year, from the GaBi database and other sources. GaBi software and CML method was used for the environmental impact assessment. Abiotic depletion potential (ADP), acidification potential (AP), eutrophication potential (EP), global warming potential (GWP) and human toxicity potential (HTP) were calculated. The results showed that electricity is the main contributor to all environmental impact categories for both slaughterhouse (with 74.36% for HTP, 73.63% for ADP, 59.61% for AP and more than 50% for EP and GWP) and processing plant (with 97.95% to AP, 96.51% to GWP, 95.49% to HTP, 94.20% to EP and 83.23% to ADP). The values for most impact categories decrease (AP, EP and GWP) when the energy is obtained by renewable sources as solar photovoltaic.

articleTitle: Scientometric Analysis of Research Trends in Nano Patches for Insulin Monitoring: Insights from Web of Science Using VOSviewer
abstract: This study conducts a scientometric analysis of the research landscape surrounding nano patches for insulin monitoring, utilizing data from the Web of Science. The analysis employs VOSviewer software to visualize and interpret the trends, publications, authorship, and citation networks in this emerging field. By examining the growth of publications over time, key research themes, and influential authors and institutions, this study aims to identify the current state of research and potential future directions in the development of nano patches for diabetes management. The findings reveal a gap in publications over last five years. Key topics identified include drug delivery mechanisms, sensor technology, and the integration of smart technologies in diabetes care. The analysis highlights the interdisciplinary nature of this field, emphasizing collaborations between materials science, biomedical engineering, and clinical research. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the research trajectory in nano patches for insulin monitoring, offering insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers in diabetes management.

articleTitle: A Brief Review on EEG-Based Diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease Using Deep Learning Models
abstract: It is obvious that early and precise detection of Parkinson's disease (PD) is crucial to avoid the progress in this neurodevelopmental brain disease. To assess PD diagnosis quantitatively, there is a growing interest in PD detection by analyzing electroencephalogram (EEG) signals using neural deep learning methods. In this study, a short review over the methods which have been used in PD diagnosis either in end-to-end approaches (e.g., deep neural network structures) or extracting informative time-frequency features from EEG signals and then apply these feature images to deep learning methods. This review addresses the challenges and offer new solutions to overcome them.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Device for Hearing Rehabilitation
abstract: Hearing loss impacts over 5% of the world's population, a percent rising due to aging populations, noise exposure, and chronic health conditions. To address this, we developed a non-invasive hearing device designed for individuals with hearing challenges that limit the use of hearing aids. The proposed device integrates a set of Bluetooth headphones with a smartphone, that process the ambient sound in real time through a software application and delivers to the hear impaired patient via bone conduction, bypassing traditional auditory pathways. Laboratory tests confirmed that the proposed device effectively replicates auditory perception. The developed device offers an accessible and user-friendly alternative to patients who cannot use traditional hearing aids.

articleTitle: Modeling Phosphate Anions Biosorption by Green Marine Algae Biomass
abstract: This study presents the modeling of phosphate anions retention by green marine algae (Ulva intestinalis), which provides information related to the mechanism of the biosorption process. The isotherm models used for the mathematical analysis of the experimental data were the Langmuir, Freundlich and Temkin models, while pseudo-first order, pseudo-second order and intra-particle diffusion models were used for the kinetic modeling. The results of the isotherm modeling show that the retention of phosphate anions occurs in a monomolecular layer, according to the Langmuir model <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.9789, \mathrm{q}_{\max}=181.81$</tex> mg/g). From a kinetic point of view, biosorption is best described by the pseudo-second order kinetic model <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.9994, \mathrm{c}_{0}=47.58$</tex> mg/L, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{k}_{2}=3.008\min^{-1},\mathrm{q}=10.52$</tex> mg/g close in value to the experimentally determined qexp = 10.50 mg/g).

articleTitle: Monitoring Health Traffic Participants Using a IoT Smart Band Integrated with a Data Collection Platform Secured with Blockchain
abstract: This work presents the development of a system aimed at providing early detection of critical heart conditions in traffic participants with cardiovascular diseases. The primary goal is to prevent traffic incidents by continuously monitoring vital signs such as heart rate heart rate (BPM) and blood oxygen level (SpOz). The proposed system represents the first medical approach of the CD data collection platform (CD Platform), integrated with an IoT Fitbit smart band (FSB), specifically designed to collect and secure health data. This prototype system provides real-time tracking and transmission of vital signs to the CD Platform, where the data is stored securely using blockchain technology to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of sensitive medical information. The collected data is used further to analyze the relationship between BPM, SpOz and traffic behavior patterns, ultimately aiding in the development of strategies and technologies to prevent incidents in cardiac patients. Preliminary results from this prototype demonstrate that the system successfully detects significant variations in BPM and SpOz were observed across different activity modes (walking, running, and driving). These findings suggest the potential of this system to be further developed as a real-time medical alert tool, enhancing patient safety

articleTitle: Preliminary Results on Designing Mechatronic Devices for Pelvic Muscles Floor Assessment
abstract: Accurate assessment of pelvic floor muscles is crucial for diagnosis and developing effective treatment plans. However, the ideal environment or access to medical devices for thorough evaluation is not always available. This article presents the concept of utilizing a Foley catheter as part of a device designed to measure pelvic floor muscle activity. The fluid column from the balloon port can be used to measure the pressure generated by muscle activity at the catheter's tip by applying Bernoulli's Equation along with an appropriate sensorial system. This allows the catheter to maintain its primary function while serving as a tool to assess the pelvic area without the need for specialized facilities or trained medical personnel. Early diagnosis and treatment can be achieved, benefiting both patient outcomes and medical efficiency. The main determinations of the necessary sensory characteristics were based on simulations and real data from pelvic muscle activation in clinical practice.

Author Keywords: pressure wave propagation in a pipe

articleTitle: Inhibitor-Driven Reaction-Diffusion Algorithm for Retinal Image Segmentation and Blood Flow Visualization
abstract: This paper proposes a segmentation algorithm for retinal images by utilizing a reaction-diffusion system of the FitzHugh-Nagumo type mathematical model. The model describes propagation of an excited state along nerve axon by a time-evolving differential equation. The equation is tuned to a bi-stable system having two stable steady states, and its bi-stability is utilized for segmentation of a retinal image into two areas: blood vessel and its background. The algorithm is applied to sample images of open datasets, and it is found that strong inhibitory coupling drives segmentation process along blood vessels and the algorithm is also applicable to blood flow visualization.

articleTitle: Retention of Rifaximin from Aqueous Solution by Adsorption on PET Fibers
abstract: In this study, the adsorption of rifaximin (initial concentration 211 mg/L) from aqueous solution on PET fibers was analyzed. The influence of five experimental parameters (pH, fiber amount, initial concentration of antibiotic, contact time and temperature) on the adsorption efficiency was examined in batch systems. The best experimental conditions for the adsorption process were determined, and these are: pH = 2.0, 0.01 g PET fibers/25 mL of aqueous solution, a contact time of 3 hours, and ambient temperature (22 °C). Under these conditions, the maximum adsorption capacity is 14.08 mg/g. The isotherm modeling of the experimental data indicates that the adsorption of rifaximin on PET fibers is a multilayer process which occurs predominantly through physical interactions (according with the Freundlich models). These results highlight the potential applications of this adsorption process in both environmental engineering and medicine fields.

articleTitle: Predicting the Time from Diagnosis to Treatment in Breast Cancer
abstract: Recent advancements in machine learning (ML) have significantly impacted the medical field, particularly in diagnosing and treating breast cancer. This study models the time from diagnosis to treatment for breast cancer patients, focusing on delay factors and ML-based solutions. The goal is to develop precise ML models that predict treatment delays, thereby improving the quality and efficiency of medical services. We investigated socio-economic disparities affecting treatment access and developed models to predict these delays. The predictive models used include K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, Linear Regression, and Boosting Algorithms such as AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting Regressor. By accurately predicting the interval from diagnosis to the first treatment, our work aims to promote equity in healthcare, ensuring timely treatment for all patients. Our findings highlight the potential of ML in optimizing treatment timelines and resource allocation, contributing to improved patient outcomes and advancing the medical system.
